Definition: from G1364 and G1540; two hundred:--two hundred.
BiblicalUsage: Two hundred is a round number the Gospels use to measure what seems impossible. Two hundred pennyworth of bread would not feed the crowd, the ship holds two hundred and seventy-six souls in all, and the two witnesses prophesy for a thousand two hundred and threescore days.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that two hundred is the number of our insufficiency. The disciples counted the cost and found it short, and that is exactly where Jesus begins, because His provision never starts with what we have.
